R code for: Miller, E. J., Steward, B. A., Witkower, Z., Sutherland, C. A. M., Krumhuber, E. G., & Dawel, A. (2023). AI hyper-realism: Why AI faces are perceived as More real than human ones. *Psychological Science.*
Contact details: amy.dawel@anu.edu.au

The analyses herein are for Miller et al.'s (2023) - reanalysis of Nightingale, S. J., & Farid, H. (2022). AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy. *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 119*(8), e2120481119.

# Load R packages 

Here, we load the required R packages.

```{r, setup, include = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

#clear workspace
rm(list = ls())

#list packages 
lib <- (c("rmarkdown", #RStudio markdown
          "knitr", #generating RStudio output
          "readr", #read in data
          "kableExtra", #extra tools for styling kable tables in R markdown knit
          "tidyverse", #also loads ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, readr, purrr, tibble
          "Hmisc", #miscellaneous          
          "psych", #core psychology functions e.g. ANOVA
          "psycho", #for signal detection analyses
          "apaTables", #for APA table output
          "lme4", #linear modelling
          "rstatix", #for checking outliers
          "ggpubr", #for publishable plots
          "ggpmisc" #stat_fit_glance function
          ))

#load packages
for (i in 1:length(lib)){
  pkg <- lib[i]
library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
}

#turn off scientific notation
options(scipen = 999)

#set date for file saving
dt <- Sys.Date()

```

# Load datasets

Here, we load the datasets from OSF for the original Nightingale & Farid
(2022) experiments 1 and 3.

Note, we have changed the variable labels so that:

-   Letter 1 = real or synthetic (r or s)

-   Letter 2 = black or east asian or south asian or white (b or e or s
    or w)

-   Letter 3 = male or female (m or f) Number = stimulus number from
    1-50

-   Suffix .acc or .trust = accuracy (for real/synthetic decision) in
    Exp 1 & 2 or trust in Exp 3

partID = participant ID within experiment

partEth = participant ethnicity (1 = Black or African American; 2 = East
Asian; 3 = Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin; 4 = Middle Eastern or
North African; 5 = South Asian; 6 = White; 98 = Other; 99 = Prefer not
to say)

NOTE: Expt3 data also include participant ethnicity data provided by
Sophie Nightingale to Amy Dawel in December 2022.

```{r, load-data}

#load datasets
df.e1 <- read.csv("../data/NF_Expt1_acc_raw_data.csv")
df.e1 <- as.data.frame(df.e1)
df.e1.summary <- read.csv("../data/NF_Expt1_acc_summary_data.csv")
df.e1.summary <- as.data.frame(df.e1.summary)
df.e2 <- read.csv("../data/NF_Expt2_acc_raw_data.csv")
df.e2 <- as.data.frame(df.e2) 
df.e2.summary <- read.csv("../data/NF_Expt2_acc_summary_data.csv")
df.e2.summary <- as.data.frame(df.e2.summary)
df.e3 <- read.csv("../data/NF_Expt3_trust_raw_data.csv") #includes participant ethnicity data provided by Sophie Nightingale to Amy Dawel December 2022
df.e3 <- as.data.frame(df.e3)

```

## Select participants for analysis

Here, we select all, White, or Black participants for the analyses.

```{r, select-sample}

#In dataset: 1 = Black or African American; 2 = East Asian; 3 = Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin; 4 = Middle Eastern or North African; 5 = South Asian; 6 = White; 98 = Other; 99 = Prefer not to say
samp = "All" #set to White, Black, or All

```

Here, we select the data for Expt1 and then run all analyses before selecting the data for Expt2 and running the exact same analyses. 

See: https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/reuse-chunks.html#ref-label

### Compute scores

Here, we compute Expt1 or Expt2 scores for each of the face types.

```{r, compute-scores-e1or2, eval = FALSE}
df.e1or2 <- df.e1or2 %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  #sum correct trials for White faces
    mutate(rwf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(swf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(swm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rw.acc = rwf.acc + rwm.acc,
           sw.acc = swf.acc + swm.acc) %>%
  #count N trials
    mutate(rwf.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(swf.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rwm.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(swm.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rw.Ntrials = rwf.Ntrials + rwm.Ntrials,   
           sw.Ntrials = swf.Ntrials + swm.Ntrials) %>%
  #compute percent accuracy
    mutate(rwf.accPc = (rwf.acc/rwf.Ntrials)*100, 
           swf.accPc = (swf.acc/swf.Ntrials)*100, 
           rwm.accPc = (rwm.acc/rwm.Ntrials)*100, 
           swm.accPc = (swm.acc/swm.Ntrials)*100, 
           rw.accPc = (rw.acc/rw.Ntrials)*100, 
           sw.accPc = (sw.acc/sw.Ntrials)*100) %>%
  #compute percent human responses                
    mutate(rwf.HumPc = rwf.accPc, 
           swf.HumPc = 100-swf.accPc, 
           rwm.HumPc = rwm.accPc, 
           swm.HumPc = 100-swm.accPc, 
           rw.HumPc = rw.accPc, 
           sw.HumPc = 100-sw.accPc) %>%
  #compute percent hits, correct rejections, false alarms, and misses
    mutate(hit.w.Pc = rw.HumPc,
           cr.w.Pc = sw.accPc, 
           fa.w.Pc = 100-cr.w.Pc, 
           miss.w.Pc = 100-hit.w.Pc) %>%
  #sum correct trials for Black faces
    mutate(rbf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rbf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sbf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("sbf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rbm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rbm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sbm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("sbm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rb.acc = rbf.acc + rbm.acc,                
           sb.acc = sbf.acc + sbm.acc) %>%
  #count N trials
    mutate(rbf.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("rbf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(sbf.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("sbf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rbm.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("rbm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(sbm.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("sbm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rb.Ntrials = rbf.Ntrials + rbm.Ntrials,    
           sb.Ntrials = sbf.Ntrials + sbm.Ntrials) %>%
  #compute percent accuracy
    mutate(rbf.accPc = (rbf.acc/rbf.Ntrials)*100, 
           sbf.accPc = (sbf.acc/sbf.Ntrials)*100, 
           rbm.accPc = (rbm.acc/rbm.Ntrials)*100, 
           sbm.accPc = (sbm.acc/sbm.Ntrials)*100, 
           rb.accPc = (rb.acc/rb.Ntrials)*100, 
           sb.accPc = (sb.acc/sb.Ntrials)*100) %>%
  #compute percent human
  mutate(rbf.HumPc = (rbf.acc/rbf.Ntrials)*100, 
         sbf.HumPc = (100-(sbf.acc/sbf.Ntrials)*100), 
         rbm.HumPc = (rbm.acc/rbm.Ntrials)*100, 
         sbm.HumPc = (100-(sbm.acc/sbm.Ntrials)*100), 
         rb.HumPc = (rb.acc/rb.Ntrials)*100, 
         sb.HumPc = (100-(sb.acc/sb.Ntrials)*100)) %>%
  #compute percent hits, correct rejections, false alarms, and misses
    mutate(hit.b.Pc = (rb.acc/rb.Ntrials)*100, 
           cr.b.Pc = (sb.acc/sb.Ntrials)*100) %>%
    mutate(fa.b.Pc = 100 - cr.b.Pc, 
           miss.b.Pc = 100 - hit.b.Pc) %>%
  #sum correct trials for East Asian faces
    mutate(ref.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("ref0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sef.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("sef0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rem.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rem0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sem.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("sem0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(re.acc = ref.acc + rem.acc,
           se.acc = sef.acc + sem.acc) %>%
  #count N trials
    mutate(ref.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("ref0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(sef.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("sef0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rem.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("rem0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(sem.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("sem0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(re.Ntrials = ref.Ntrials + rem.Ntrials,  
           se.Ntrials = sef.Ntrials + sem.Ntrials) %>%
  #compute percent accuracy
    mutate(ref.accPc = (ref.acc/ref.Ntrials)*100, 
           sef.accPc = (sef.acc/sef.Ntrials)*100, 
           rem.accPc = (rem.acc/rem.Ntrials)*100, 
           sem.accPc = (sem.acc/sem.Ntrials)*100, 
           re.accPc = (re.acc/re.Ntrials)*100, 
           se.accPc = (se.acc/se.Ntrials)*100) %>%
  #compute percent human
  mutate(ref.HumPc = (ref.acc/ref.Ntrials)*100, 
         sef.HumPc = (100-(sef.acc/sef.Ntrials)*100), 
         rem.HumPc = (rem.acc/rem.Ntrials)*100, 
         sem.HumPc = (100-(sem.acc/sem.Ntrials)*100), 
         re.HumPc = (re.acc/re.Ntrials)*100, 
         se.HumPc = (100-(se.acc/se.Ntrials)*100)) %>%
  #compute percent hits, correct rejections, false alarms, and misses
    mutate(hit.e.Pc = (re.acc/re.Ntrials)*100, 
           cr.e.Pc = (se.acc/se.Ntrials)*100) %>%       
    mutate(fa.e.Pc = 100 - cr.e.Pc, 
           miss.e.Pc = 100 - hit.e.Pc) %>%
  #sum correct trials for South Asian faces
    mutate(rsf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rsf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(ssf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("ssf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rsm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rsm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(ssm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("ssm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rs.acc = rsf.acc + rsm.acc,
           ss.acc = ssf.acc + ssm.acc) %>%
  #count N trials
    mutate(rsf.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("rsf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(ssf.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("ssf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rsm.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("rsm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(ssm.Ntrials = sum(!is.na(across(starts_with("ssm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rs.Ntrials = rsf.Ntrials + rsm.Ntrials,
           ss.Ntrials = ssf.Ntrials + ssm.Ntrials) %>%
  #compute percent accuracy
    mutate(rsf.accPc = (rsf.acc/rsf.Ntrials)*100, 
           ssf.accPc = (ssf.acc/ssf.Ntrials)*100, 
           rsm.accPc = (rsm.acc/rsm.Ntrials)*100, 
           ssm.accPc = (ssm.acc/ssm.Ntrials)*100, 
           rs.accPc = (rs.acc/rs.Ntrials)*100, 
           ss.accPc = (ss.acc/ss.Ntrials)*100) %>%
  #compute percent human
  mutate(rsf.HumPc = (rsf.acc/rsf.Ntrials)*100, 
         ssf.HumPc = (100-(ssf.acc/ssf.Ntrials)*100), 
         rsm.HumPc = (rsm.acc/rsm.Ntrials)*100, 
         ssm.HumPc = (100-(ssm.acc/ssm.Ntrials)*100), 
         rs.HumPc = (rs.acc/rs.Ntrials)*100, 
         ss.HumPc = (100-(ss.acc/ss.Ntrials)*100)) %>%
  #compute percent hits, correct rejections, false alarms, and misses
    mutate(hit.s.Pc = (rs.acc/rs.Ntrials)*100, 
           cr.s.Pc = (ss.acc/ss.Ntrials)*100) %>% 
    mutate(fa.s.Pc = 100 - cr.s.Pc, 
           miss.s.Pc = 100 - hit.s.Pc) 

```

### Calculate signal detection measures

Here, we calculate signal detection measures.

```{r, compute-SDT-e1or2, eval = FALSE}
#from: https://www.r-bloggers.com/2018/03/compute-signal-detection-theory-indices-with-r/
#also see: https://people.brandeis.edu/~sekuler/stanislawTodorov1999.pdf

sdt.w <- psycho::dprime(n_hit = df.e1or2$hit.w.Pc,
                        n_fa = df.e1or2$fa.w.Pc, 
                        n_miss = df.e1or2$miss.w.Pc, 
                        n_cr = df.e1or2$cr.w.Pc)
df.e1or2 <- cbind(df.e1or2, sdt.w)
df.e1or2 <- df.e1or2 %>% 
  rename(dprime.w = dprime, 
         beta.w = beta, 
         aprime.w = aprime, 
         bppd.w = bppd, 
         c.w = c)

sdt.b <- psycho::dprime(n_hit = df.e1or2$hit.b.Pc,
                        n_fa = df.e1or2$fa.b.Pc, 
                        n_miss = df.e1or2$miss.b.Pc, 
                        n_cr = df.e1or2$cr.b.Pc)
df.e1or2 <- cbind(df.e1or2, sdt.b)
df.e1or2 <- df.e1or2 %>% 
  rename(dprime.b = dprime, 
         beta.b = beta, 
         aprime.b = aprime, 
         bppd.b = bppd, 
         c.b = c)

sdt.e <- psycho::dprime(n_hit = df.e1or2$hit.e.Pc,
                        n_fa = df.e1or2$fa.e.Pc, 
                        n_miss = df.e1or2$miss.e.Pc, 
                        n_cr = df.e1or2$cr.e.Pc)
df.e1or2 <- cbind(df.e1or2, sdt.e)
df.e1or2 <- df.e1or2 %>%
  rename(dprime.e = dprime,
         beta.e = beta, 
         aprime.e = aprime, 
         bppd.e = bppd, 
         c.e = c)

sdt.s <- psycho::dprime(n_hit = df.e1or2$hit.s.Pc,
                        n_fa = df.e1or2$fa.s.Pc, 
                        n_miss = df.e1or2$miss.s.Pc, 
                        n_cr = df.e1or2$cr.s.Pc)
df.e1or2 <- cbind(df.e1or2, sdt.s)
df.e1or2 <- df.e1or2 %>%
  rename(dprime.s = dprime, 
         beta.s = beta, 
         aprime.s = aprime, 
         bppd.s = bppd, 
         c.s = c)

#write data to csv
write.csv(df.e1or2, paste0("../data/NF_", df.Name, "_scored_", samp, "Ps.csv"))

```

### Filter data to selected sample

Here, we filter the Expt1 or Expt2 data to our selected participant sample, as
specified at [Select participants for analysis].

```{r, filter-sample-e1or2, eval = FALSE}

if (samp == "White"){
df.e1or2.incPs <- df.e1or2 %>%
  filter(partEth == 6)
df.e1or2.summary.incPs <- df.e1or2.summary %>%
  filter(partEth == 6)
} else if (samp == "Black"){
df.e1or2.incPs <- df.e1or2 %>%
  filter(partEth == 1)
df.e1or2.summary.incPs <- df.e1or2.summary %>%
  filter(partEth == 1)
} else if (samp == "All"){
df.e1or2.incPs <- df.e1or2 
df.e1or2.summary.incPs <- df.e1or2.summary
}

```

### Distribution plots

Here, we plot variable distributions for our selected sample.

```{r, histograms-e1or2, eval = FALSE}

#reshape into wide data for plots: dprime
dfl.e1or2.dprime.incPs <- df.e1or2.incPs %>%  
  gather("var", "dprime", c(dprime.w, dprime.b, dprime.e, dprime.s), convert = TRUE)

#distribution plots
ggplot(dfl.e1or2.dprime.incPs) +
  geom_density(aes(x = dprime, colour = var)) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels=c("Black","East Asian","South Asian", "White")) +
  labs(color="Race of Face Stimuli")+
  theme_bw()

#reshape into wide data for plots: c
dfl.e1or2.c.incPs <- df.e1or2.incPs %>%  
  gather("var", "c", c(c.w, c.b, c.e, c.s), convert = TRUE)

#distribution plots
ggplot(dfl.e1or2.c.incPs) +
  geom_density(aes(x = c, colour = var)) + xlim(c(0, 3.5)) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels=c("Black","East Asian","South Asian", "White")) +
  labs(color="Race of Face Stimuli")+
  theme_bw()

#reshape into wide data for plots: accuracy
dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs <- df.e1or2.summary.incPs %>%  
  gather("var", "mean.accPc", c(rbf.accPc, sbf.accPc, rbm.accPc, sbm.accPc, ref.accPc, sef.accPc, rem.accPc, sem.accPc, rsf.accPc, ssf.accPc, rsm.accPc, ssm.accPc, rwf.accPc, swf.accPc, rwm.accPc, swm.accPc, rnb.accPc, snb.accPc), convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(face.sex = substr(var, 3, 3)) %>% #f = female, m = male, b = both
  mutate(face.race = substr(var, 2, 2)) %>% #n = nonwhite, e = east asian, s = south east asian, b = black, w = white
  mutate(face.format = substr(var, 1, 1)) #r = real, s = synthetic

dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs$face.sex <- dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs$face.sex %>%
  str_replace_all(c("m" = "Male", 
                    "f" = "Female", 
                    "b" = "Both face sexes"))

dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs$face.race <- dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs$face.race %>%
  str_replace("^n", "Non-white") %>%
  str_replace("^s", "South Asian") %>% 
  str_replace("^e", "East Asian") %>%
  str_replace("^w", "White") %>%
  str_replace("^b", "Black") 

dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs$face.format <- dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs$face.format %>%
  str_replace_all(c("r" = "Real human", 
                    "s" = "Synthetic human"))

#distribution plots
ggplot(dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs) +
  geom_density(aes(x = mean.accPc, colour = face.race)) +
  facet_wrap(~face.format*face.sex, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x="Mean Accuracy (%)", color="Race of Face Stimuli") +
  theme_bw()

#filter out non-white grouping
dfl.e1or2.wVoth.incPs <- dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs %>%
  filter(face.race != "Non-white")

#distribution plots
ggplot(dfl.e1or2.wVoth.incPs) +
  geom_density(aes(x = mean.accPc, colour = face.race)) +
  facet_wrap(~face.format*face.sex, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x="Mean Accuracy (%)", color="Race of Face Stimuli") +
  theme_bw()

ggplot(dfl.e1or2.wVoth.incPs) +
  geom_density(aes(x = mean.accPc, colour = face.format)) +
  facet_wrap(~face.race*face.sex, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x="Mean Accuracy (%)", color="Format of Face Stimuli") +
  theme_bw()

#filter out non-white grouping
dfl.e1or2.wVn.incPs <- dfl.e1or2.summary.incPs %>%
  filter(face.race != "Black") %>%
  filter(face.race != "East Asian") %>%
  filter(face.race != "South Asian")

#distribution plots
ggplot(dfl.e1or2.wVn.incPs) +
  geom_density(aes(x = mean.accPc, colour = face.race)) +
  facet_wrap(~face.format, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x="Mean Accuracy (%)", color="Race of Face Stimuli") +
  theme_bw()

```

### Test d prime, b, and c

Here, we compare dprime to 0 and b to 1 for the White faces.

```{r, dprime-ttests-e1or2, eval = FALSE}

# make the qqplot
qqnorm(df.e1or2.incPs$dprime.w)
qqline(df.e1or2.incPs$dprime.w)
t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$dprime.w, mu = 0)

qqnorm(df.e1or2.incPs$beta.w)
qqline(df.e1or2.incPs$beta.w)
t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$beta.w, mu = 0) #bias > 1 = towards saying "yes" is human

qqnorm(df.e1or2.incPs$c.w)
qqline(df.e1or2.incPs$c.w)
t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$c.w, mu = 0) #negative c = false alarms > misses

```

### Reshape wide data into long format

Here, we reshape our data into long format.

```{r, reshape-w2l-e1or2, eval = FALSE}

#subset data
dfl.e1or2.incPs <- df.e1or2.incPs %>%
  select('partID', 'rwf.accPc':'swm.accPc')

dfl.e1or2.incPs <- dfl.e1or2.incPs %>%  
  gather("var", "mean.accPc", c(rwf.accPc, swf.accPc, rwm.accPc, swm.accPc), convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(face.sex = substr(var, 3, 3)) %>%
  mutate(face.format = substr(var, 1, 1))

dfl.e1or2.incPs$face.sex <- as.factor(dfl.e1or2.incPs$face.sex)
dfl.e1or2.incPs$face.format <- as.factor(dfl.e1or2.incPs$face.format)
  
```

### ANOVA and pwc

Here, we test for differences in accuracy between real and synthetic
faces (by face sex),
following:<https://www.datanovia.com/en/lessons/mixed-anova-in-r/#three-way-bww-b>

```{r, ANOVA-e1or2, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}

#check for outliers
dfl.e1or2.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex, face.format) %>%
  identify_outliers(mean.accPc) #no outliers

#shapiro test for normality
dfl.e1or2.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex, face.format) %>%
  shapiro_test(mean.accPc) #does not meet assumption of normality

#qqplots
ggqqplot(dfl.e1or2.incPs, "mean.accPc", ggtheme = theme_bw()) +
  facet_grid(face.sex ~ face.format, labeller = "label_both") #visual = minor violations

#homogeneity of variance
dfl.e1or2.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex) %>%
  levene_test(mean.accPc ~ face.format) #meets assumption of homogeneity of variance

#ANOVA
aov.res <- anova_test(
  data = dfl.e1or2.incPs, dv = mean.accPc, wid = partID,
  within = c(face.sex, face.format)
  )
aov.out <- as.data.frame(aov.res)
print(aov.out) #sig. main effects for face.sex and face.format, but no sig. interaction

#compute pairwise comparisons
pwc <- dfl.e1or2.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex) %>%
  pairwise_t_test(
    mean.accPc ~ face.format, paired = TRUE, 
    p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"
    )
view(pwc)

```

## Pairwise comparisons

Here, we include comparisons to chance.

```{r, pwc-e1or2, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}

t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$swm.accPc, df.e1or2.incPs$rwm.accPc)

t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$sw.accPc, df.e1or2.incPs$rw.accPc)

t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$swf.accPc, mu = 50)
t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$rwm.accPc, mu = 50)

t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$sbf.accPc, mu = 50)
t.test(df.e1or2.incPs$rbm.accPc, mu = 50)
```

# Experiment 3

## Compute scores

Here, we compute Experiment 3 mean trust ratings for each of the face
types.

```{r, compute-scores-e3}

df.e3 <- df.e3 %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  #compute mean trust ratings for White faces
    mutate(rwf.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(swf.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwm.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(swm.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rw.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rw") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sw.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sw") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    #compute mean trust ratings for Black faces
    mutate(rbf.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rbf0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sbf.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sbf0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rbm.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rbm0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sbm.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sbm0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rb.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rb") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sb.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sb") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    #compute mean trust ratings for South Asian faces
    mutate(ref.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("ref0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sef.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sef0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rem.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rem0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(sem.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sem0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(re.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("re") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(se.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("se") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    #compute mean trust ratings for South Asian faces
    mutate(rsf.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rsf0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(ssf.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("ssf0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rsm.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rsm0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(ssm.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("ssm0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rs.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rs") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(ss.mean.trust = rowMeans(across(starts_with("ss") & contains ("0") & ends_with(".trust")), na.rm = TRUE)) 

#write data to csv
write.csv(df.e3, paste0("../data/NF_Expt3_scored.csv"))

```

## ANOVA and pwc

Here, we test for differences in trustworthiness between real and
synthetic faces (by face sex),
following:<https://www.datanovia.com/en/lessons/mixed-anova-in-r/#three-way-bww-b>

```{r, ANOVA-e3, include = TRUE, warning = FALSE, echo = TRUE}

#check for outliers
dfl.e3.incPs.whFaces %>%
  group_by(face.sex, face.format) %>%
  identify_outliers(mean.trust) #no outliers

#shapiro test for normality
dfl.e3.incPs.whFaces %>%
  group_by(face.sex, face.format) %>%
  shapiro_test(mean.trust) #does not meet assumption of normality

#qqplots
ggqqplot(dfl.e3.incPs.whFaces, "mean.trust", ggtheme = theme_bw()) +
  facet_grid(face.sex ~ face.format, labeller = "label_both") #visual = minor violations

#homogeneity of variance
dfl.e3.incPs.whFaces %>%
  group_by(face.sex) %>%
  levene_test(mean.trust ~ face.format) #meets assumption of homogeneity of variance

#ANOVA
aov.res <- anova_test(
  data = dfl.e3.incPs.whFaces, dv = mean.trust, wid = partID,
  within = c(face.sex, face.format)
  )
aov.out <- as.data.frame(aov.res)
print(aov.out)

#compute pairwise comparisons
pwc <- dfl.e3.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex, face.race) %>%
  pairwise_t_test(
    mean.trust ~ face.format, paired = TRUE, 
    p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"
    )
view(pwc)

```

# Using Expt1 data to predict Expt3 trust ratings

Here, we use Expt1 mean accuracy to predict
Expt3 mean trust ratings across the individual stimuli.

```{r, stimuli-means-corrs}

#select Expt1 data
if (samp == "White"){
df.e1.incPs <- df.e1 %>%
  filter(partEth == 6)
} else if (samp == "Black"){
df.e1.incPs <- df.e1 %>%
  filter(partEth == 1)
} else if (samp == "All"){
df.e1.incPs <- df.e1
}

#calculate mean accuracy for each stimulus in Expt1
df.e1.incPs.stim <- df.e1.incPs %>%
  select('rbf001.acc':'swm050.acc') %>%
  colMeans(na.rm = TRUE)

#convert to tibble and keep stimulus names
df.e1.incPs.stim <- as_tibble(df.e1.incPs.stim, rownames = NA) %>%
  rownames_to_column()

#calculate mean trustworthiness for each stimulus in Expt3
df.e3.incPs.stim <- df.e3.incPs %>%
  select('rbf001.trust':'swm050.trust') %>% 
  colMeans(na.rm = TRUE)

#convert to tibble and keep stimulus names
df.e3.incPs.stim <- as_tibble(df.e3.incPs.stim, rownames = NA) %>%
  rownames_to_column()

df.e1.e3.incPs.stim <- cbind(df.e1.incPs.stim, df.e3.incPs.stim)
colnames(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim) <- c("e1.var", "e1.acc", "e3.var", "e3.trust")
df.e1.e3.incPs.stim <- as_tibble(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim)

df.e1.e3.incPs.stim <- df.e1.e3.incPs.stim %>%
  select(-"e3.var") %>%
  mutate(face.sex = substr(e1.var, 3, 3)) %>%
  mutate(face.race = substr(e1.var, 2, 2)) %>%
  mutate(face.format = substr(e1.var, 1, 1)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(e1.prop.real = case_when(
    face.format == "r" ~ e1.acc, 
    face.format == "s" ~ 1 - e1.acc, 
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ))

df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.sex <- as.factor(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.sex)
df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.race <- as.factor(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.race)
df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.format <- as.factor(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.format)

ggplot(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim, aes(x = e1.prop.real, y = e3.trust)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = face.format)) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm") +
  stat_fit_glance(method = "lm",
                  method.args = list(formula = y ~ x),
                       geom = "text",
                       aes(label = paste("p = ", round(after_stat(p.value),3), sep = ""))) +
  facet_wrap(~ face.race, ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels=c("Real human", "Synthetic human")) +
  labs(color="Format of Face Stimuli") +
  theme_bw()

df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.format <- df.e1.e3.incPs.stim$face.format %>%
  str_replace("^r", "Real human") %>%
  str_replace("^s", "Synthetic human") 

ggscatter(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim, x = "e1.prop.real", y = "e3.trust", facet.by = "face.race", add = "reg.line", color = "face.format", conf.int = TRUE, cor.coef = TRUE, cor.method = "pearson") %>%
  ggpar(legend.title = "Format of Face Stimuli")

ggplot(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim, aes(factor(face.format), e1.prop.real)) +
  geom_violin(draw_quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) +
  facet_wrap(~ face.race, ncol = 1)

ggplot(df.e1.e3.incPs.stim, aes(factor(face.format), e3.trust)) +
  geom_violin(draw_quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) +
  facet_wrap(~ face.race, ncol = 1)

df.e1.e3.incPs.stim %>%
  group_by(face.race) %>%
  summarise(corrs = cor(e1.prop.real, e3.trust))

```
